items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a seminormed ring $ R $, this function returns a sequence indexed by $ \mathbb{N} $ where each term is defined as $ \|p_n\|^{1/(d - n)} $ if $ n < d $, and $ 0 $ otherwise. Here, $ p_n $ denotes the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $, $ d $ is the natural degree of $ p $, and $ \|\cdot\| $ is the seminorm on $ R $. This sequence captures the normed coefficients' growth rates relative to their distance from the polynomial's degree.

items.informal_name: Definition of Roth Number Function on Natural Numbers
items.type: ∀ (n : ℕ), rothNumberNat n = addRothNumber (Finset.range n)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the Roth number function $ \text{rothNumberNat}(n) $, which gives the maximum size of a subset of $ \{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\} $ containing no three distinct elements forming an arithmetic progression, is equal to $ \text{addRothNumber}(\text{range } n) $.

items.informal_name: Witt Polynomial Expressing Xₙ in Terms of W
items.type: (p : ℕ) → (R : Type u_1) → [inst : CommRing R] → [Invertible ↑p] → ℕ → MvPolynomial ℕ R
items.informal_description: For each natural number $n$, the polynomial $X_n$ is defined recursively as $\left(X_n - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} p^i \cdot \text{W}_i^{p^{n-i}}\right) \cdot p^{-n}$, where $\text{W}_i$ denotes the Witt polynomial for index $i$, $p$ is an invertible element of the commutative ring $R$, and $p^{-n}$ is its inverse raised to the $n$-th power. This expresses the variable $X_n$ in the polynomial ring $\mathbb{N} \to R[\mathbb{N}]$ as a combination of lower-index Witt polynomials scaled by powers of $p$ and its inverse.

Each term in the product is the multiplicative inverse of the difference between $ v_i $ and $ v_j $.

items.informal_name: Preservation of Finite Infima by Infimum- and Top-Preserving Maps
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {F : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : CompleteLattice α] [inst_1 : CompleteLattice β]
  [inst_2 : FunLike F α β] [InfTopHomClass F α β] [Finite ι] (f : F) (g : ι → α), f (⨅ i, g i) = ⨅ i, f (g i)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be complete lattices, and let $\iota$ be a finite type. For any function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ that preserves infima and top elements (i.e., $f$ is an $\inf$- and $\top$-homomorphism), and for any indexed family $g : \iota \to \alpha$, the following equality holds: $$ f\left(\bigwedge_{i \in \iota} g(i)\right) = \bigwedge_{i \in \iota} f(g(i)). $$

items.informal_name: Infimum Degree Invariance under WithTop Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {T : Type u_4} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : SemilatticeInf T] [inst_2 : OrderTop T]
  {D : A → T} {s : AddMonoidAlgebra R A},
  s.support.Nonempty → AddMonoidAlgebra.infDegree (WithTop.some ∘ D) s = ↑(AddMonoidAlgebra.infDegree D s)
items.informal_description: For a non-empty finite support element $ s $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[A] $, the infimum degree computed using the degree function $ D $ composed with the $ \text{WithTop} $ embedding equals the infimum degree computed directly with $ D $. Formally, $ \infdegree (\top \circ D) s = \infdegree D s $, where $ \top $ denotes the canonical embedding of $ A $ into $ \text{WithTop}(A) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Infimum with Infimum-Preserving Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [inst : SemilatticeInf α] [inst_1 : OrderTop α]
  [inst_2 : SemilatticeInf γ] [inst_3 : OrderTop γ] {s : Finset β} {f : β → α} (g : α → γ),
  (∀ (x y : α), g (x ⊓ y) = g x ⊓ g y) → g ⊤ = ⊤ → g (s.inf f) = s.inf (g ∘ f)
items.informal_description: Let $\gamma$ be an infimum semilattice with top element $\top$. For any finite set $s \subseteq \beta$, function $f : \beta \to \alpha$, and function $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ that preserves infima ($g(x \sqcap y) = g(x) \sqcap g(y)$) and the top element ($g(\top) = \top$), it holds that $g$ applied to the infimum of $f(s)$ equals the infimum of $g \circ f(s)$. Symbolically: $g\left(\bigwedge_{b \in s} f(b)\right) = \bigwedge_{b \in s} g(f(b))$.

items.informal_name: Preservation of Infimum under Function Mapping for Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {F : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : CompleteLattice α] [inst_1 : CompleteLattice β]
  [inst_2 : FunLike F α β] [InfTopHomClass F α β] {s : Set ι},
  s.Finite → ∀ (f : F) (g : ι → α), f (⨅ x ∈ s, g x) = ⨅ x ∈ s, f (g x)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $, if $ f $ is an infimum and top-preserving homomorphism between complete lattices $ \alpha $ and $ \beta $, then $ f $ applied to the infimum of $ g(x) $ over $ s $ equals the infimum of $ f(g(x)) $ over $ s $. Symbolically: $ f\left(\bigwedge_{x \in s} g(x)\right) = \bigwedge_{x \in s} f(g(x)) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum-Top Homomorphism Preserves Infimum over Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {F : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} [inst : SemilatticeInf α] [inst_1 : OrderTop α]
  [inst_2 : SemilatticeInf β] [inst_3 : OrderTop β] [inst_4 : FunLike F α β] [InfTopHomClass F α β] (f : F)
  (s : Finset ι) (g : ι → α), f (s.inf g) = s.inf (⇑f ∘ g)
items.informal_description: For a function $ f $ preserving infima and the top element, the image of the infimum of a finite set $ s $ under $ f $ is equal to the infimum of the images of the elements of $ s $ under $ f $, i.e., $ f\left(\bigwedge_{b \in s} g(b)\right) = \bigwedge_{b \in s} f(g(b)) $.
